profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between Orion's orchestration owner and the security researcher responsible for target onboarding, held the afternoon before an overnight benchmark run on four remaining open-source libraries including clib. The context is that Orion has separate workstreams for auto-generating fuzz harnesses and for scheduling, artifact collection, and crash triage automation, and the team needs to align on what Ethan will hand off today and what Priya's pipeline will consume tonight. The agenda is to confirm the clib target handoff, check whether the target is ready for the overnight cluster slot, and confirm where triage outputs will appear for morning review. The expected outcome is an apparently smooth agreement on deliverables, target version, run readiness, and triage handoff for the overnight campaign.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.role: Staff Platform Engineer for Orion Orchestration
members.expertise: CI/CD systems, containerized build pipelines, distributed job scheduling, artifact management
members.background: Priya built Orion's evaluation runner and maintains the benchmark snapshot repository, cluster scheduler integration, and the artifact manifests used to launch automated fuzzing campaigns.
members.private_state: She wants tonight's run to be fully automated with no manual exceptions, keep all targets on the pinned benchmark snapshot for reproducibility, and avoid introducing special-case packaging logic that would slow down the orchestration workstream.
hidden_assumptions: When people say a target name like 'clib', they mean the pinned benchmark snapshot revision in the benchmarks-2024Q4 repo unless a different commit is explicitly called out.
A 'campaign package' is the launchable artifact boundary for her team: an OCI image digest plus target.yaml manifest fields that the scheduler can consume.
A target is 'ready for overnight' once it builds cleanly and survives the standard 20-minute smoke fuzzing check on one shard without harness-level failures.
The triage handoff from the platform side consists of raw crashing inputs, stack traces, and metadata automatically written to the run bucket; downstream interpretation happens later.

members.name: Ethan Cole
members.expertise: Coverage-guided fuzzing, harness design, sanitizer debugging, crash triage, vulnerability validation
members.background: Ethan leads the target-analysis side of Orion, adapting generated harnesses for real libraries, tuning seed corpora and dictionaries, and validating whether crashes are worth reporting.
members.private_state: He wants the overnight run to maximize the chance of finding publishable vulnerabilities, keep the ability to use the newest upstream fixes that make harnessing easier, and avoid wasting time on noisy crash sets that still need heavy manual triage in the morning.
hidden_assumptions: When a library target like 'clib' is discussed informally, it refers to the latest upstream branch he has been iterating on, not the older benchmark snapshot, unless someone explicitly says 'snapshot.'
A 'campaign package' is the researcher-facing deliverable: the harness source folder with its seed corpus, dictionary, sanitizer knobs, and notes, which the platform side can build from.
A target is 'ready for overnight' only if it has shown stable sanitizer behavior and meaningful coverage growth over a multi-hour dry run, not merely a short smoke test.
The useful triage handoff is a minimized reproducer set with deduped logs and brief annotations, because raw crash artifacts are not yet actionable findings.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to handing off 'the campaign package' for clib.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means a launch-ready OCI image plus target.yaml manifest that the scheduler can ingest directly.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the harness folder in the repo with source, seed corpus, dictionary, and fuzzing notes that can later be built into a runnable target.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see packaging as a routine handoff artifact and each assumes their own layer is the obvious, standard interpretation, so the shared term creates a strong sense of alignment without anyone enumerating contents.

misalignment_points.topic: Which clib revision is 'the clib target'
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about using 'the clib target' or 'the same clib target as last week.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 is thinking of the pinned benchmark snapshot in benchmarks-2024Q4 at commit 9f2c1b7, which her scheduler synced yesterday.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 is thinking of his working upstream branch based on clib main at commit 7d81aa2, which includes a parser refactor that made the harness stable.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: There is only one salient clib effort on each person's dashboard, and in benchmark-heavy workflows target names are usually treated as stable identifiers, so neither person feels the need to cite the exact commit.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree that clib should be 'ready for the overnight run.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the target compiles, the manifest validates, and a 20-minute smoke fuzzing job on one shard shows no immediate harness crashes or infrastructure issues.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the target has already survived a several-hour dry run, shown sustained coverage growth beyond initial seed replay, and had flaky sanitizer crashes filtered out.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase sounds like a shared operational milestone, and both parties are competent enough that each assumes the other applies the same common-sense readiness bar without spelling out the test threshold.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to reviewing 'the triage bundle' from the overnight run in the shared bucket.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 expects the run bucket to contain Orion's automatic triage output: raw crashing inputs, ASan logs, stack traces, and metadata grouped by signature.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 expects the bundle he reviews in the morning to already include minimized reproducers, deduplicated crash sets, and short bug notes suitable for filing.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both use the same artifact location and the same noun for post-run outputs, but each mentally includes the steps owned by their own workstream inside that bundle, so the scope difference remains invisible.

If that holds, Orion can absorb it like every other target and I don't have to introduce any one-off packaging path.
